stemMd: The student wants to emphasise the size of the difference between the two groups of marshes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Because decay proceeds slowly in their waterlogged soil, tidal marshes store carbon, which Vrbova measured in restored marshes in 2023.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Marshes restored over 30 years earlier held 4.6 kilograms of carbon per square metre, nearly four times the 1.2 kilograms in those restored under 10 years earlier.

options.label: C
options.textMd: In 2023, ecologist Hana Vrbova surveyed 32 restored tidal marshes along a single coastline, some restored under 10 years earlier and some over 30.

options.label: D
options.textMd: After surveying 32 restored tidal marshes along one coastline in 2023, Vrbova concluded that carbon storage in a restored marsh builds up slowly, over decades.

explanationMd:
A rhetorical-synthesis item is scored against the stated goal, not against general quality. The goal here is to emphasise *the size of a difference*, so the winning sentence must put both figures side by side and make the gap visible.

The choice putting both figures side by side does all of that: it gives 4.6 kg/m² and 1.2 kg/m², and it quantifies the relationship. Check the multiplier: $4.6 \div 1.2 \approx 3.83$, so "nearly four times" is accurate and does not overstate the notes.

To check any synthesis answer, underline the goal's key words — here "the size of the difference" — and confirm the sentence gives both sides of the comparison with a figure for each. Naming the two groups is not enough; only one choice states how much carbon each group stored.

distractorRationale.a: Accurate, but it gives background on how marshes store carbon and on when Vrbova measured it, and mentions neither group of marshes. A sentence with no comparison in it cannot emphasise the size of a difference.
distractorRationale.c: Accurate, but it emphasises the scope of the survey — the year, the 32 sites and the ages of the marshes sampled. It names the two groups without saying how much carbon either stored, so it shows who was compared, not how large the difference was.
distractorRationale.d: This states the conclusion drawn from the difference rather than the difference itself. "Slowly, over decades" describes the pattern qualitatively, and the survey details add scope, not size: the sentence includes neither of the two storage figures.

accessibilityText: Using the five student notes about carbon in restored tidal marshes, choose the sentence that best emphasises the size of the difference between marshes restored recently and marshes restored long ago. The four choices say: that because decay proceeds slowly in their waterlogged soil, tidal marshes store carbon, which Vrbova measured in restored marshes in 2023; that marshes restored over 30 years earlier held 4.6 kilograms of carbon per square metre, nearly four times the 1.2 kilograms in those restored under 10 years earlier; that in 2023 ecologist Hana Vrbova surveyed 32 restored tidal marshes along a single coastline, some restored under 10 years earlier and some over 30; and that after surveying 32 restored tidal marshes along one coastline in 2023, Vrbova concluded that carbon storage in a restored marsh builds up slowly, over decades.

independentSolve.workingNotes: 4.6 / 1.2 is about 3.83, so 'nearly four times' is accurate, and B is the only option that quantifies the difference. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-sat-rw-run1) reached the same answer: 4.6/1.2 = 3.83, so 'nearly four times' is accurate, and B is the only choice that quantifies the gap between the two groups. A, C and D give context or the conclusion without the size of the difference.]
